Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Make the link clear. In Lesson 2, the information was given to them on practice notices and a practice website. In Lesson 3 they do the research themselves: search, choose a good source, write notes, double-check, then talk about it with the teacher. These are the skills they need for the VU23562 project.

Today: three big steps

Find itSearch online.
Choose a good source.
Note itWrite the details in a table.
Double-check them.
Talk about itAnswer your teacher's questions about the place.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
The lesson title has three parts, and the lesson follows them. Find it: Stop 5 (good sources). Note it: Stop 6 (notes in a table) and Stop 7 (a trip planner). Talk about it: Stop 8 (a talk with your teacher). Ask: Have you ever looked for information about a place online? What did you look for?

Lesson 3: your route

Today we start at stop 1
Stop 1Talk first: Coco and Liu look for a community centre.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Walk the route with the class. Click a stop to show what it is about. Lesson 3 has 9 stops: talk first (listening), everyday expressions, Say it (teen and ty numbers, dates and short forms), grammar (three tenses, questions and time words), research it, note it, routes and stops on a trip planner, talk about it with your teacher, and check your learning. Activity 27 is homework: students find their own route to the college on a trip planner app.

Stand up if you have ever ...

been to a community centre
used a trip planner app
called the council
joined a club or a group
visited a JP
caught a ferry in Sydney
Ask: Have you ever been to a community centre? ↗  Answer: Yes, I have. ↘ / No, I haven't. ↘
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Read each card as a question: "Have you ever been to a community centre?" Students stand up if the answer is yes. Ask one standing student a follow-up in the past simple: Which one? When did you go? This previews the new tense in Lesson 3, the present perfect for experience. A JP is a Justice of the Peace, who can sign and certify documents for free. Do not teach the grammar yet: Stop 4 does that.

How long have you lived here?

1
Which suburb do you live in?
2
How long have you lived there?
3
How long have you been in Australia?
Example: I've lived in Cammeray for two years. I've lived there since 2024.
Look at the example. What comes after for? After since?
for + a length of time: for two years, for six months
since + a start point: since 2024, since March
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs. Suburb only, never a street address. Model with your own answer first. Let pairs guess the for / since pattern, then click the button. This previews the second use of the present perfect in Lesson 3 (how long), which comes back in Stop 4 and in the Stop 8 talk with the teacher.

Strong = louder and longer
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Say each word yourself, or click the gold speaker button (the computer voice is a back-up only). Students clap on the strong syllable, then click Show. Answers: nine-TEEN (strong at the end, long sound), NINE-ty (strong at the start), LONG-uh-ville, al-ex-AN-der, WAY-ver-ton. Teen and ty numbers are a big focus in Stop 3; this pair (19 / 90) is not in the worksheet drill, so Activity 9 stays fresh.

Not sure? Check it!

Sorry, can you say that again?
Do you mean 15 or 50?
How do you spell that?
So it's on Tuesdays, right? ↗
Game: your teacher reads some information about a place. Use a check question to be sure!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Drill each check question. Voice goes up at the end of "So it's on Tuesdays, right?" Game: say practice details quickly, for example "The pool's at 13 Burns Bay Road, open Thursdays from 4:15." Students must check: Do you mean 13 or 30? Tuesday or Thursday? This is the Lesson 3 conversation technique (Stop 1), and it is very useful in the talk with the teacher.

Everyday talk: guess it!

Guess with your partner first. Then listen for these words today!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs guess the meaning from the example sentence. You can hold the answers until after the Talk first conversation, or click now if the group needs support. All four are in the Coco and Liu conversation and in Activity 5. The other four new expressions (spot on, fair enough, sorted, too easy) stay as a surprise for the worksheet.

Is it a good source?

You need the opening hours of a pool. Where do you look?
the council website
the pool's own website
a call to the front desk
a map app
a forum post from 2017
an ad for a swim school
Tip: Two sources say different things? Double-check! Look at a second source or call.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs decide: good source or not? Then click Show. Good: the council website, the pool's own website, a phone call, a map app (but map apps can be old, so double-check). Not good: an old forum post (old, and just someone's opinion) and an ad (it wants to sell you something). This previews Stop 5, Research it, and the search results in Activity 18.
